jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Cloud Product Engineering
jobs.description:
Aerospike is powering the next generation of real-time, massive-scale applications—and we need an exceptional Director of Engineering to build the gateway to it all. You will own the vision, architecture, and execution for how thousands of developers and enterprise teams interact with, pay for, and observe the Aerospike Cloud Platform.

This isn't just about managing code; it’s about shaping the entire developer journey across our multi-cloud, multi-tenant ecosystem. You will lead the charge on everything from lightning-fast UI/API experiences to complex usage-based monetization and real-time telemetry pipelines handling massive data flows.

To foster strong alignment and execution, Bay Area–based leaders are expected in-office Tuesday through Thursday.

We need a high-octane strategic leader who loves big technical challenges, thrives on building high-impact teams, and stays close enough to the tech to drive serious architectural authority. Partnering directly with executive leaders in Product, Design, Finance, and Infrastructure, you will transform complex, distributed database capabilities into an effortless, intuitive, and wildly reliable cloud service.

What You’ll Do

Build & Scale a World-Class Org: Empower, mentor, and grow a premier organization of engineering managers, technical leads, and full-stack/frontend engineers. Drive a high-velocity culture rooted in innovation, autonomy, and delivery.
Revolutionize the Customer Experience: Define the multi-year vision for our developer consoles, APIs, and user-facing workflows—ensuring every interaction with Aerospike Cloud is fast, friction-free, and delightful.
Architect the Core Business Engine (BLT):

Monetization & Usage: Spearhead the architectural evolution of our high-volume billing engines, real-time usage tracking, and multi-cloud marketplace integrations (AWS, GCP, Azure, Stripe).
Licensing & Entitlements: Build bulletproof, multi-tenant entitlement systems and feature-gating frameworks designed for global enterprise scale.
Telemetry & Observability: Drive the strategy for deep, real-time observability (metrics, logs, traces) that turns billions of platform events into actionable insights for both our engineers and customers.

Drive Technical Excellence: Serve as the ultimate bar-raiser for microservices architecture, API design, and modern frontend systems. Keep the tech stack cutting-edge while eliminating complexity.
Align Tech with Business Growth: Translate big-picture enterprise strategy into clear, executable technical roadmaps alongside Product, Revenue, and Executive Leadership.
Own Production Reliability: Establish non-negotiable standards for billing precision, sub-second interface performance, and enterprise-grade SLA availability in a 24/7/365 cloud environment.

What We’re Looking For

10+ years scaling customer-facing SaaS, PaaS, or cloud infrastructure platforms at serious velocity.
4+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience, with a proven track record of managing managers, scaling teams, and leading through technical leads.
Domain Powerhouse: Deep expertise in architecting cloud monetization engines (metered billing, marketplace integrations) and high-throughput telemetry/observability platforms (OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Prometheus).
Deep Technical DNA: Hands-on foundation in modern web stacks (React, TypeScript), scalable API design (REST, GraphQL), and cloud-native infrastructure (Kubernetes, Go, multi-cloud platforms).
Executive Presence & Business Acumen: A clear, compelling communicator who seamlessly connects deep technical architecture to revenue strategy, product execution, and executive goals.
Battle-Tested Operational Ownership: Proven experience running high-availability, mission-critical production systems where downtime or inaccuracy is not an option.

Nice to Have

Experience building developer consoles, control planes, or management interfaces for NoSQL databases, data platforms, or high-throughput infrastructure.
Direct experience leading engineering through periods of rapid scaling, enterprise transformations, or major cloud platform expansions.
Hands-on familiarity with distributed systems, event-driven architectures, or technologies like Temporal and Node.js.
Familiarity with distributed systems or high-scale databases.

Salary Range

: $272,000 – $350,000

(Actual compensation will be based on experience, location, and other relevant factors.)

Aerospike is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We are committed to an environment free from discrimination based on race, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, or veteran status.

To keep our recruitment pipeline as high-performance as our database, Aerospike uses AI-driven tools to streamline resume reviews, scheduling, and communication. While we love smart tech, we value human connection even more. AI helps us optimize the process, but real people make 100% of the actual hiring decisions.

Aerospike is the real-time database for mission-critical use cases and workloads, including machine learning, generative, and agentic AI. Aerospike powers millions of transactions per second with millisecond latency, at a fraction of the total cost of ownership compared to other databases.

Global leaders, including Adobe, Airtel, Barclays, Criteo, DBS Bank, Experian, Grab, HDFC Bank, PayPal, Sony Interactive Entertainment, The Trade Desk, and Wayfair, rely on Aerospike for customer 360, fraud detection, real-time bidding, profile stores, recommendation engines, and other use cases.

At Aerospike, we dream big and deliver even bigger. Our mission is to unleash the power of the world’s real-time data

with a database built for infinite scale, speed, and sustainability

.

If you're ready to shape the future of data, join us.

jobs.description:
Description

Role Summary

The Director, AI & Automation leads the team responsible for building and scaling the organization's automation and agentic AI capabilities. This role owns a team of engineers working across two closely related domains: workflow orchestration and deterministic automation, and agentic coding practices and AI-enabled engineering.

This is a high-autonomy, high-accountability role at the leading edge of how the organization applies AI to internal operations. The Director is expected to be a practitioner and a leader - someone who understands the technology deeply enough to make good engineering decisions, develop strong engineers, and contribute meaningfully to how the organization thinks about AI adoption and governance over time.

Essential Functions

Lead a team of engineers across agentic AI and workflow automation disciplines, organized into self-directed pods aligned to business domains; ensure pods are staffed, enabled, and delivering effectively.
Own engineering quality and technical standards across both workflow orchestration and deterministic automation, as well as agentic AI tooling and practices.
Drive adoption of agentic coding practices across the team - establishing patterns, evaluating emerging approaches, and building engineering fluency in AI-assisted development at scale.
Partner with Product Owners embedded in each pod to ensure engineers have clear priorities, well-defined work, and the technical context needed to deliver effectively.
Ensure continuous rapid evaluation of automation tooling, frameworks, and agentic patterns, bringing well-reasoned recommendations to leadership and contributing to governance conversations as a technical voice.
Participate in AI governance and definition of responsible AI frameworks, helping to establish standards for how the organization deploys, monitors, and evaluates AI-driven automation in production.
Manage the full engineer lifecycle across the team - hiring, onboarding, performance, growth, and retention - with particular attention to developing engineers in a fast-moving and ambiguous technology domain.
Maintain visibility into pod delivery across all business domains; surface risks, capacity issues, and cross-pod dependencies to leadership before they become blockers.
Represent the AI & Intelligent Automation engineering function in cross-functional conversations with technology leadership, business stakeholders, and vendor partners.

Qualifications & Skills

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field. Equivalent experience accepted.
6+ years of experience in technology, engineering, or IT operations, with at least 2 years managing large teams.
Demonstrated ability to lead engineers or technical teams working in fast-moving, ambiguous domains where standards and practices are still being established.
Working knowledge of workflow automation and orchestration concepts - understanding how automated processes are designed, integrated, and maintained in an enterprise environment. Hands-on experience with specific platforms is a plus but not required.
Familiarity with AI and agentic automation concepts sufficient to evaluate tooling, guide engineering decisions, and engage credibly with technical teams and leadership. Direct engineering experience in AI is a plus; genuine curiosity and the ability to learn quickly are required.
Experience managing engineers or technical staff across multiple concurrent workstreams, teams, or business domains simultaneously.
Track record of building team culture, engineering standards, or operational practices in environments where they did not fully exist before.
Strong judgment on technology evaluation - able to assess new tools and approaches against real organizational constraints, not just technical appeal.
Comfortable operating at the intersection of team leadership, technical judgment, and strategic contribution.
Strong communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences.

Location: Marlborough/ Chelmsford, MA or Hillsborough- 1+days onsite/week

Target Compensation: $180,400 - $216,700

Schedule: 8am- 5pm

jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

Fermi America™ (Nasdaq & LSE: FRMI) is pioneering the world's largest next-generation private HyperGrid™ campus, Project Matador, located on approximately 8,400 acres in the Texas Panhandle near Amarillo. The campus is designed to deliver up to 17 gigawatts of highly redundant, behind-the-meter power to hyperscale artificial intelligence data centers, integrating the nation's largest combined-cycle natural gas generation complex, utility-scale solar PV, battery energy storage systems (BESS), utility grid interconnection, and one of the most ambitious nuclear power programs in the United States.

With first power targeted for 2027 and nearly $1 billion in committed financing secured, Fermi America is one of the most consequential energy infrastructure companies in the United States. The Head of Engineering is a critical leadership role at the heart of this mission.

ROLE PURPOSE

The Head of Engineering is Fermi America's senior technical authority and Owner's Engineer for Project Matador's HyperGrid™ campus. This executive owns the engineering standards, design basis, and technical decisions for the program from conceptual design and front-end engineering design (FEED) through detailed engineering, construction support, commissioning, and handover to operations. Detailed engineering is executed by Fermi America's contracted engineering partners and EPC contractors; the Head of Engineering directs, reviews, approves, and holds those partners to account across a multi-technology portfolio spanning gas-fired generation, high-voltage transmission and substations, campus utilities, data center power infrastructure, and battery energy storage, with utility-scale solar PV and nuclear generation in future phases.

The role builds and leads a corporate engineering organization of Principal discipline engineers who serve as Fermi America's subject matter experts, owns the Engineering Management System, leads the technical interfaces with EPC contractors, engineering partners, OEMs, and the interconnecting utility (SPS/Xcel), and ensures all engineering deliverables meet Fermi America's safety, quality, regulatory, schedule, and performance requirements. The group is fully capable of performing design where Fermi America elects to do so; its primary function is owner-side technical leadership of the partners who execute the work.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering Leadership & Strategy

Define and own the engineering strategy for Project Matador, ensuring technical coherence across gas-fired generation, high-voltage transmission, data center power, BESS, and future solar PV and nuclear systems.
Establish and enforce engineering standards, codes of practice, design criteria, and design verification requirements across all disciplines, coordinated with the Director of Quality, who owns QA/QC.
Lead the engineering organization structure, resource planning, and capability development to support the phased delivery of up to 17 GW of generation capacity.
Provide technical vision and leadership to the COO, executive leadership, and Board on engineering risk, innovation, and delivery strategy.
Champion a safety-by-design culture, embedding HSSE requirements into all engineering deliverables from concept through commissioning.

Power Generation Engineering: Gas & BESS

Provide owner technical direction and oversight of the combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) program engineered by Fermi America's EPC and engineering partners, including Siemens Energy and GE gas turbines, heat recovery steam generators (HRSGs), steam turbines, and associated balance-of-plant systems.
Direct and approve battery energy storage system (BESS) sizing and integration engineering performed by Fermi America's engineering partners, including containerized battery systems, inverters, thermal management, protection and control, and grid integration.
Review and approve FEED and detailed engineering packages, technical specifications, equipment datasheets, and vendor drawings from EPC contractors and OEMs.
Provide engineering support to Procurement and Commissioning for factory acceptance testing (FAT) of major equipment and for resolution of technical punch list items through commissioning completion.

High-Voltage Electrical & Grid Engineering

Direct and approve the engineering of the campus's high-voltage transmission and distribution infrastructure, performed by Fermi America's HV engineering partner in coordination with SPS/Xcel, including substations, switching stations, overhead lines, underground cables, and protection and control systems.
Direct grid interconnection engineering, including system impact studies, protection coordination, power flow analysis, and SPS/Xcel interconnection technical deliverables, including large load interconnection studies.
Set the electrical design basis for the campus grid interface to data center power infrastructure (substations, switchgear, and transformers) and provide engineering review in support of Data Center Delivery, which owns the data center electrical scope including UPS systems and standby generation.
Ensure grid and power system engineering complies with NERC reliability standards, SPS/Xcel interconnection requirements, and applicable IEEE and ANSI codes.

Controls, SCADA & Digital Engineering

Own the design basis and architecture of the campus-wide Distributed Control System (DCS), SCADA, and Energy Management System (EMS) architecture.
Lead the development of control system philosophies, cause-and-effect matrices, alarm management strategies, and cybersecurity frameworks for operational technology (OT) in accordance with NERC CIP standards.
Direct the digital twin strategy for generation asset monitoring, predictive maintenance, and operational optimization.
Ensure seamless integration of all generation technologies (gas, BESS, grid interconnection, and future solar PV and nuclear) into the campus EMS/SCADA platform.

Civil, Structural & Site Engineering

Oversee civil and structural engineering for all generation facilities, campus utilities, substations, transmission structures, data center foundations, and site-wide infrastructure.
Direct geotechnical, environmental, and hydrological engineering studies and ensure findings are incorporated into design standards.
Manage the engineering interface with Site Infrastructure, Construction, HSSE and Permitting, and Data Center Delivery to ensure designs are constructable, cost-effective, and permit-compliant.

Future Phase Generation: Nuclear & Solar PV

Serve as the senior engineering interface for Fermi America's nuclear program as it advances, working with nuclear technology vendors, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), and specialist nuclear engineering consultants; oversee engineering inputs to NRC license applications, safety analysis reports, and site characterization studies in accordance with applicable NRC regulations, ANSI/ANS standards, and DOE requirements.
Plan the internal nuclear engineering capability required to support pre-licensing, design certification, and later construction and operations phases, scaled to program timing.
Direct owner oversight of utility-scale solar PV engineering when that phase is initiated, including array design, DC/AC power conversion, substation integration, and SCADA connectivity.

EPC, Engineering Partner & OEM Technical Management

Lead the technical review and approval of EPC contractor and engineering partner deliverables, ensuring compliance with Fermi America's engineering standards and project specifications.
Perform the Owner's Engineer function, acting as Fermi America's technical authority in disputes, claims, and technical variation assessments in support of Operations' contractor commercial management.
Maintain technical interfaces with key OEM partners for gas generation, solar module and inverter suppliers, BESS manufacturers, and nuclear technology vendors.
Oversee engineering sign-off as required on construction completion, pre-commissioning, commissioning, and performance testing milestones.

Regulatory & Permitting Engineering

Provide engineering support to Fermi America's HSSE and Permitting organization for federal, state, and local permitting, including SPS/Xcel interconnection filings, TCEQ air quality permits, NRC license applications, and Texas PUC filings.
Ensure engineering deliverables support Fermi America's TCEQ air permit applications and amendments, environmental impact assessments, and grid code compliance documentation.
Liaise with regulatory agencies at the technical level and represent Fermi America's engineering position in regulatory proceedings.

Engineering Management System & Standards

Establish and maintain the Engineering Management System, including design review and verification processes, management of change (MOC), and document control.
Own engineering risk registers and lead technical risk workshops at key project milestones.
Define and enforce engineering standards for all disciplines, ensuring alignment with applicable US codes (ASME, IEEE, ANSI, NFPA, API, NEC) and international standards where applicable.
Lead lessons-learned processes and drive continuous improvement in engineering performance across the program.

Requirements

Essential

Bachelor's degree or higher in Engineering.
15+ years of progressive engineering experience in the power generation or energy infrastructure sector, with at least 7 years in a senior engineering leadership role.
Deep technical expertise in combined-cycle gas turbine power plants and in high-voltage transmission and substations, with working knowledge of battery energy storage systems and data center power infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary engineering organizations on major capital projects ($500M+ CAPEX).
Strong track record of managing EPC contractor engineering deliverables, Owner's Engineer functions, and OEM technical interfaces.
Owner-side experience directing multiple concurrent engineering partners and EPC contractors on a single program, including technical authority over their deliverables.
Professional Engineer (PE) license in Texas or ability to obtain reciprocal licensure.
Experience with transmission service provider interconnection engineering, including large load interconnection studies with a utility such as SPS/Xcel, NERC reliability standards, and US power system codes (IEEE, ANSI, NFPA, NEC).

Desirable

Experience with nuclear power engineering, NRC licensing processes, or advanced nuclear technology development (SMR, Gen IV).
Experience with utility-scale solar PV engineering and grid integration.
Familiarity with NERC CIP cybersecurity standards for operational technology and industrial control systems.
Experience with behind-the-meter private grid design and multi-technology hybrid power system integration.
MBA or major project leadership qualification (e.g., PMP, APM PMQ).
Experience working on first-of-a-kind or gigawatt-scale energy infrastructure programs in the United States.

Compass Technology is a dedicated internal team for Compass Group delivering enterprise-wide initiatives that support our diverse customer base and enhance our business operations. Our domain encompasses a vast spectrum of opportunities, from hands-on desk support to Cybersecurity, Cloud Engineering, AI, and Modern Application development. We are committed to building robust IT infrastructures, driving digital transformation, and much more.

Job Summary

Reporting to the Sr. Director of Cybersecurity within Compass Group North America, the Director of Security Engineering owns the strategy, leadership, and execution of Compass Group’s security engineering functions across cloud security, infrastructure security, and detection engineering. Leading a multi-team organization, the Director sets the technical roadmap for security controls across cloud environments and the security tooling and infrastructure underpinning our security operations.

The role owns the health and effectiveness of our security tooling, the detection engineering function that turns telemetry into high-fidelity, actionable signals, and the cloud security capabilities that deploy and maintain controls across our multi-cloud footprint. It is highly collaborative, partnering closely with the Incident Management, Identity Management, Exposure Management, Security Architecture, and Security Administration teams within the CISO Office, and with technology teams across Compass Group North America.

Job Responsibilities

jobs.title: Director, Systems and Electro-Optical Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

Position Title:
Director, Systems and Electro-Optical Engineering

Position Description:
Protingent Staffing has an exciting direct hire Director, Systems and Electro-Optical Engineering opportunity.

Job Description:

Looking for a Director of Systems and Electro-Optical Engineering to lead the group that defines how our LiDAR sensors are architected, specified, and optically realized. The role brings systems architecture, systems engineering, optical design, and laser engineering under one leader, so that the trade-offs between optical design choices and system-level performance requirements are owned in one place rather than negotiated across teams.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role. The Director owns the product architecture and requirements baseline, leads a team of senior individual contributors, and is the system-level technical authority for the sensor within Engineering. The role partners with the Chief Scientist on technology direction and with the VP of Engineering on program execution. The scope may expand over time as the organization grows.

Job Responsibilities

Systems Architecture: Own the end-to-end sensor architecture: requirements decomposition, interface definition, and system-level trade studies across optical, laser, electronic, mechanical, and software subsystems. Establish and maintain the product specification and interface baseline where it does not yet exist, and govern it where it does.
Electro-Optical Design: Lead optical design and laser engineering as an integral part of systems architecture. Own the trade-offs between beam characteristics, transmit and receive optics, laser parameters, and system performance (range, resolution, object separability, signal-to-noise, eye safety).
Sensing Strategy and Requirements: Own the system-level requirements and acceptance criteria for how the sensor scans and samples the scene, including how sensor output is consumed by downstream perception systems. Firmware and software teams implement against these requirements; this role defines them.
Team Leadership: Lead, mentor, and grow a team of senior individual contributors spanning systems architecture, systems engineering, optical design, and laser engineering. Set technical standards, calibrate performance, and build the ladder from Systems Engineer through Principal levels.
Cross-Functional Alignment: Act as the system-level interface between Hardware, Firmware, Software, Product, Quality, and Operations. Drive root-cause analysis of system-level and electro-optical failures.
Requirements Management: Establish requirements management that traces customer and product requirements to architecture and design decisions across the product lifecycle.
Technical Governance: Chair system-level design reviews and gate reviews. Ensure design decisions are documented, change-controlled, and traceable to requirements.
Program Execution: Partner with Program Management and the VP of Engineering to set technical milestones, manage technical risk, and deliver systems and electro-optical work products on program schedules from prototype through production.
Customer and Executive Engagement: Represent the systems and electro-optical capability in customer technical reviews, and report architecture health, technical risk, and resourcing needs to the VP of Engineering and, as needed, the executive team.

Job Qualifications:

10+ years of engineering experience in electro-optical or sensor systems, with at least 4 years leading senior individual contributors or engineering teams.
Proven track record architecting and shipping electro-optical sensing products (LiDAR, imaging, ranging, photonics, or similar) from concept through production.
Depth in at least one of optical design or laser engineering, and fluency in the other, sufficient to own trade-offs across both.
Strong systems engineering fundamentals: requirements decomposition, interface control, and design review governance.
Experience establishing a requirements and architecture baseline in a company that did not yet have one, and transitioning designs from prototype to production under change control.
Experience with electro-optical and system-level failure analysis.
Excellent cross-functional leadership and communication, with the ability to translate technical detail for executive and customer audiences.
Bachelor's degree in Optical Engineering, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

Preferred Job Qualifications

Experience with scanning LiDAR architectures and their interaction with downstream perception software.
Familiarity with laser safety standards (IEC 60825) and with functional safety or sensor qualification standards (ISO 26262, automotive or aerospace environmental qualification).
Experience with high-reliability electronics and single-point-failure analysis for demanding environments.
Experience scaling an engineering function within a growth-stage hardware company.
Experience presenting to boards, investors, or enterprise customers on technical roadmaps.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering |PM Hotel Group |Hilton Garden Inn Opryland Nashville
jobs.description:
What You’ll Do:

We want you to look after this hotel as if it were your home. You'll make sure broken things get fixed, and more importantly, you'll create a detailed program to ensure they don't break in the first place. From the little everyday details - maintenance of our guestrooms, public space, and the back of the house - to the big capital plans that help our hotels maintain their fresh appeal, you'll schedule, direct, and follow up to ensure each project reaches completion. You'll make sure we have the right tools and equipment and keep them organized, and that chemicals and hazardous materials are used and stored properly. You'll make sure work is performed safely and efficiently.

Here are some of the tasks you will complete on a daily basis:

Troubleshoot and repair malfunctions in mechanical or electrical systems (e.g., HVAC, plumbing) and other equipment throughout the hotel.
Perform preventative maintenance assignments on a scheduled basis.
Lead, manage and communicate information about capital projects and property rehabilitation.
Communicate with hotel department heads to become aware of maintenance needs and ensure timely response to internal requests.
Hire, train, evaluate, and lead all maintenance staff.

Where You’ve Been:

You have at least 3 years of management or supervisory experience in a hotel and have experience with several areas such as HVAC, electrical, carpentry, dry walling, painting, plumbing, roofing, and landscaping. You’re able to perform in a high-paced environment with multiple tasks and deadlines and able to effectively respond to emergencies.

When You’re Here:

Although you’ll sometimes be behind the desk, be prepared to move around because you will be standing/sitting, carrying/lifting up to 50 pounds, walking, bending/twisting, climbing stairs and more. Be prepared to be on call at all times in case of emergency including nights, weekends, and holiday. But wait, there’s a great upside: in exchange for your flexibility, we offer excellent pay, hotel discounts, F&B discounts and the opportunity to be part of an anything-but-standard growing hotel company.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Software Development, WW Sustainability
jobs.description:
Description

Join us at the forefront of Amazon's sustainability initiatives to work on environmental and social advancements to support Amazon's long term worldwide sustainability strategy. At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people.

The Worldwide Sustainability (WWS) organization capitalizes on Amazon’s scale and speed to build a more resilient and sustainable company. We manage our social and environmental impacts globally, and drive solutions that enable our customers, businesses, and the world to become more sustainable.

Amazon's Worldwide Sustainability team is building the science and technology infrastructure that makes our sustainability commitments real — auditable, automated, and actionable at Amazon's scale. At the center of that infrastructure is the Carbon Intelligence Platform: the system that calculates emissions across Amazon's businesses, powers planning and abatement decision-making, and serves external sustainability products for partners and customers outside Amazon.

We are looking for a Senior Manager, Software Development to lead the engineering team building and operating this platform. This is a player-coach role — you will set technical direction, manage and grow a team of engineers, and stay close enough to the code and architecture to make the hard technical calls yourself. You will own production systems that business unit leaders, finance teams, and external partners depend on for numbers they report publicly and use to make consequential decisions.

This role sits at a distinctive intersection: technical depth and organizational scope at the same time. You will partner with research and sustainability scientists whose methodologies — increasingly AI and ML-enabled — your team implements in production. You will own an external-grade API surface that commercial sustainability products depend on to serve customers outside Amazon. And you will build an AI-native engineering team: one that builds AI/ML systems in production *and* uses AI-assisted development and testing as standard workflow, measuring success by the pace at which new capabilities reach customers reliably.

Your ability to communicate and influence others will be a key to success. You are a results-oriented, customer-focused manager who gets excited about diving deep, running hard, and delivering a big impact.

Key job responsibilities

Carbon Intelligence Systems

Every carbon calculation that any Amazon business unit or external partner relies on runs through systems you own and operate
External-grade API surface consumed by commercial sustainability products — versioned, rate-limited, documented, and reliable at external SLAs
Assurance & Decision-making: All data must be fully explainable to assurance providers, external stakeholders and enable rapid decision making
Carbon Facts and Assumptions

Engineering & People Leadership

Lead a team of software development engineers directly; this is an level 7 player-coach role with hands-on technical involvement
Set technical direction and architecture — API design, system reliability, AI/ML production infrastructure, and technical debt management
Own the engineering operating model: production reliability, incident response, deployment practices, and on-call
Own model serving infrastructure, inference pipelines, model observability, and automated retraining pipelines
Drive AI-native engineering practices: AI-assisted development and testing as standard workflow, measured by velocity and reliability of customer-facing delivery
Hire, develop, and retain strong engineering talent

Science-to-Production Boundary

Receive methodology and model specifications from the science team and build the production infrastructure that makes them reliable at scale
Triage production failures independently and surface systematic patterns back to the science team on a defined cadence

differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (inclusive diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Experience managing multiple concurrent programs, projects and development teams in an Agile environment
Experience building and operating production API platforms at scale — versioning, SLA management, external-grade documentation, and reliability engineering
Experience building and operating AI/ML production systems — model serving, inference pipelines, drift detection, and retraining automation

Data is the foundation of autonomous driving. Every improvement in Nuro’s autonomy stack depends on identifying the right real-world examples, transforming them into high-quality training and evaluation datasets, and rigorously validating that each software release is ready for the road.

As Head of Software Operations, you will lead the organization responsible for this critical development loop—from producing the data that trains and evaluates Nuro’s AI models to identifying autonomy regressions and building confidence in every software release. Sitting at the center of Nuro’s autonomy organization, your team will work closely with machine learning, autonomy, simulation, onboard systems, data science, and product teams. You will also help Nuro take advantage of emerging technologies, including multimodal foundation models, LLMs to improve how training data is created and how system performance is evaluated.

We are looking for a proactive, technically fluent operational leader who can identify gaps across the autonomy development lifecycle and build the teams, systems, and partnerships needed to close them. jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.

Hiring And How We Work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Senior Engineering Manager.

About The Job

As a Senior Engineering Manager in Communication Identity Domain, you will lead the engineering teams behind Porting, Hosting, and A2P Messaging. Your teams own the products that let customers bring their own numbers onto Twilio (Porting), enable existing numbers for messaging without a full port (Hosting), and register and operate compliant Application-to-Person (A2P) messaging campaigns at scale — the gateway that determines whether a customer's messages actually reach their end users' handsets. Porting and Hosting are high-value, white-glove transactions: each one touches an existing customer's live production number, or a prospective customer's number that already works elsewhere and needs to keep working seamlessly through the transition. That makes operational maturity a core part of the value we deliver — precise execution, clear communication, and dependable outcomes are what earn a customer's trust in the Communication Identity Domain. Delivering on that requires deep, reliable integration with a broad ecosystem of carriers, aggregators, industry registries and the expertise to orchestrate that complexity into a smooth, trustworthy experience for the customer. It also means investing in efficient, well-instrumented Ops Tooling that gives your team and our internal support organizations clear visibility into every port, hosting activation, and campaign — so issues are caught and resolved quickly, and operational excellence scales with the business. You will own the people strategy, delivery execution, and stakeholder relationships for a team responsible for the trust-building work of moving and activating phone numbers for existing and prospective customers.

You will be expected to champion AI-driven development practices, ensuring your engineers adopt LLMs and agentic tools to accelerate delivery, improve quality, and stay at the forefront of modern software engineering. Your mission is to build a high-performing team that consistently ships reliable, customer-obsessed products - while balancing the competing demands of external product commitments, internal platform obligations, and operational tooling investments.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

DRAW THE OWL: Own the delivery roadmap for the Communication Identity Domain, including customer-facing services, internal platform APIs, and Ops Tooling. Partner with Principal and Staff Engineers to translate long-term technical strategy into executable quarterly plans and measurable outcomes.
ACCELERATE WITH AI: Drive the adoption of AI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, Anthropic Claude, or internal LLMs) within your team. Set expectations for AI-augmented workflows, measure the impact on team velocity, and create the psychological safety for engineers to experiment with new tools.
BE AN OWNER: Take full accountability for your team’s operational excellence, including system reliability, incident response, on-call health, and security posture. Make high-judgment calls that balance speed, quality, and risk.
WEAR THE CUSTOMER’S SHOES: Serve two customer bases with equal rigor. For external customers, partner with Product Management to ensure communication identity workflows are seamless and developer-friendly. For internal customers, proactively engage with dependent engineering teams to understand their needs, gather feedback on your team’s APIs and Ops Tooling, and ensure your platform enables them to move faster. Ground every decision in customer data and feedback from both audiences.
EMPOWER OTHERS: Recruit, develop, and retain a world-class engineering team. Build a culture of psychological safety, candid feedback, and career growth. Coach your engineers-from mid-level to staff-to reach their full potential and take on increasing ownership. Champion diversity, equity, and inclusion in every hiring and development decision.
RUTHLESSLY PRIORITIZE: Navigate competing priorities across external product features, internal platform needs, and Ops Tooling investments. Balance requests from multiple stakeholders-Product Management, internal engineering teams, and operations-with a clear framework for saying “no” to protect focus. Ensure resources are aligned to the highest-impact work across all three pillars.
WRITE IT DOWN: Communicate team strategy, progress, and risks clearly and consistently to engineering leadership and cross-functional partners. Author team plans, post-mortems, and decision documents that create transparency and alignment.
BUILD BRIDGES: Act as the primary point of contact between the Communication Identity Domain and its stakeholders. Manage relationships with Product Management, external-facing teams, and internal engineering teams that depend on your services and Ops Tooling. Proactively communicate roadmap plans, surface trade-offs, negotiate priorities, and ensure stakeholders have clear visibility into what your team is delivering and why.
NO SHENANIGANS: Model integrity in every interaction. Create an environment where engineers feel safe raising concerns, surfacing problems early, and challenging the status quo. Hold yourself and your team to the highest standards of ethical behavior.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

Required:
15+ years of software engineering experience with at least 5+ years in engineering management, leading a team of 10+ engineers and directly managing individual contributors.
Technical Depth: Strong hands-on background in designing and operating highly available, cloud-native distributed systems. You don’t need to write code daily, but you MUST be able to engage deeply in architectural reviews, evaluate technical proposals, and earn the trust of your senior engineers.
Cloud-Native Fluency: Deep familiarity with AWS ecosystems (Lambda, EKS, DynamoDB, Kafka), microservices patterns, and infrastructure-as-code practices (Kubernetes, Terraform).
AI-Forward Mindset: Demonstrated experience driving AI tool adoption within your engineering team. You should be able to articulate a clear vision for how AI accelerates your team’s delivery and quality.
Delivery Excellence: Proven track record of shipping complex software products on time and at high quality. Experience with agile methodologies and a data-driven approach to measuring team health and productivity.
People Leadership: A track record of building diverse, inclusive, high-performing engineering teams. Experience with career frameworks, performance management, and growing engineers from mid-level to staff-plus.
Clear Communication: Strong ability to communicate technical strategy, trade-offs, and team plans to engineering leadership, cross-functional partners, and your direct reports.
Stakeholder Management: Proven ability to manage relationships across multiple stakeholder groups with competing needs. Experience balancing external customer commitments with internal platform obligations and communicating trade-offs transparently.
Operational Rigor: Experience owning system reliability for mission-critical services, including incident management, on-call rotations, and SLO-driven operational improvements.

Desired

Platform & Tooling Leadership: Experience leading a team that builds internal platforms or operational tooling serving other engineering teams, with a product mindset toward internal customers.
Team Scaling: Experience growing and evolving a team through periods of change, including onboarding new engineers, reshaping team processes, and managing through ambiguity.

Location

This role will be remote, but is not eligible to be hired in San Francisco, CA, Oakland, CA, San Jose, CA, or the surrounding areas.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Compensation

Please note this role is open to candidates outside of California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Vermont, Washington D.C., and Washington State. The information below is provided for candidates hired in those locations only.

The estimated pay ranges for this role are as follows:

Based in Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Vermont or Washington D.C. : $207,200.00 - $259,000.00
Based in New York, New Jersey, Washington State, or California (outside of the San Francisco Bay area): $219,360.00 - $274,200.00.
Based in the San Francisco Bay area, California: $243,680.00 - $304,600.00.
This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio’s equity plan and corporate bonus plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Application deadline information

Applications for this role are intended to be accepted until 30th November, but may change based on business needs.

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud

We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. jobs.title: Sr. Software Development Manager, Relational Database Services
jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) is one of the fastest growing services in AWS, running millions of customer databases across every commercial and sovereign region. Keeping those databases current, secure, and healthy at that scale is one of the hardest and most consequential problems in managed databases. Our vision is to provide the best in class release and patch management available.

We are looking for a Senior Software Development Manager to build the next generation of how RDS patches, upgrades, and manages the software lifecycle of every database we operate.

You will lead multiple engineering teams reinventing how we deliver operating system, engine, and platform software updates to customer fleets, with the goal of making patching and upgrades a best-in-class, low-touch, and trustworthy experience. You will own the strategy and delivery of advanced patching and upgrade systems designed for the next generation of the cloud: safer automation, richer customer control, and near-zero-downtime maintenance. You will set the multi-year technical vision, hire and grow a strong org, and partner across RDS, database engines, and AWS security to raise the bar on how customers keep their databases current.

The right leader is equally comfortable defining strategy in ambiguity and diving deep into the mechanics of fleet-wide software delivery. You think in terms of customer trust, operational safety, and long-term platform leverage, and you build teams that ship durable systems rather than one-off fixes.

Key job responsibilities

Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for RDS patching, upgrades, and software lifecycle management across the entire managed fleet.
Build and lead several engineering teams delivering net-new systems for advanced patching and upgrade orchestration, safety, and automation.
Raise the bar on maintenance safety: minimize customer-visible downtime, expand automated validation and rollback, and shorten the time from CVE disclosure to fleet-wide remediation.
Partner with database engine, security, and operations teams to align on a coherent software lifecycle strategy for the next generation of the cloud.
Hire, develop, and retain a high-performing organization; grow managers and senior engineers and set a high standard for operational and engineering excellence.
Represent the patching and lifecycle strategy to senior AWS leadership and to customers, and drive alignment on long-term direction.

A day in the life

You spend your morning in a design review for a new upgrade-orchestration system, pushing the team on how it behaves during partial failure and how it earns customer trust. Midday you review fleet health and remediation metrics with your leads, decide where to invest to raise the bar on critical patch SLAs, and unblock a cross-team dependency with the engine teams. In the afternoon you work with a principal engineer on the multi-year lifecycle vision, then meet with a manager on their team's hiring and growth plans. Throughout, you are balancing near-term operational commitments against the net-new platform you are building.

About The Team

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS? Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

10+ years of engineering experience
5+ years of engineering team management experience
10+ years of planning, designing, developing and delivering consumer software experience
Experience partnering with product or program management teams
Experience managing multiple concurrent programs, projects and development teams in an Agile environment

Description

A Senior Forward Deployed Engineering Manager (Senior FDE Manager) leads multiple pods of FDEs across several strategic enterprise customers, defining the delivery model, engineering standards, and talent strategy for the FDE practice at scale. This is not a Solutions Architect management role and not a consulting engagement manager role. Senior FDE Managers own organizational-level outcomes — they set the technical direction across multiple concurrent customer programs, build and scale the FDE team, and drive the mechanisms that ensure consistent engineering excellence and measurable business impact across the entire portfolio.

Senior FDE Managers operate at org-level scope. They lead 15–30+ engineers, influence technical decisions across multiple customer engagements and AWS teams simultaneously, and define what "great" looks like for forward-deployed AI engineering management. They represent the FDE practice to AWS senior leadership and customer C-suite executives, balancing strategic vision with operational execution.

Lead the FDE delivery organization. Own delivery across multiple customer engagements and FDE pods. Staff and structure teams for optimal customer coverage. Define engagement models, staffing strategies, and delivery cadences. Ensure consistent engineering quality across all active programs. Requires 30 – 50% travel.
Define technical strategy and standards. Set the technical direction for the most complex customer AI programs spanning your organization. Align technical strategy with adjacent AWS teams. Be a key influencer for strategic decisions, bringing technology and industry context to business decisions. Resolve escalations and drive closure with peers, Directors, and stakeholders.

Accelerate transformation at portfolio level. Identify systemic opportunities to expand AI adoption across multiple customer organizations. jobs.title: Head of Infrastructure Security Engineering - EDA Clusters
jobs.description:
Securing NVIDIA’s EDA clusters is not a matter of deploying the standard security stack. These workloads are too large, too long-running, and too performance-sensitive for the off-the-shelf playbook to simply apply. That constraint is the job. We’re hiring an engineering leader to build and run Infrastructure Security Engineering for EDA Clusters: the team responsible for implementing security controls across the compute, storage, and networking that NVIDIA’s hardware engineers design silicon on, spanning on-prem data centers and multi-cloud environments. You’ll operate as the peer counterpart to NVIDIA’s company-wide security organization and to hardware infrastructure engineering, translating enterprise security intent into controls that hold up at EDA scale without slowing chip design down.

Much of this is a build, not a maintain. You’ll have the authority to decide where standard tooling applies, where it actively cannot, and what NVIDIA engineers instead then lead a team to do it. If your depth is in large-scale networking and compute infrastructure at a hyperscaler, a security product company, or anywhere fleets and fabrics are the day job and you’ve carried real accountability for the security properties of those systems, you are exactly who we want to talk to. We don’t expect you to arrive fluent in every security product category; we do expect you to own security outcomes from day one and to acquire the remaining domain breadth fast. Strong infrastructure mastery plus sharp security instincts beats a broad product résumé here. This is a role for someone who believes security engineering is engineering: automation, instrumentation, and secure-by-default infrastructure not tickets, exceptions, and spreadsheets.

What You’ll Be Doing

Build and lead the team. Grow and direct a team of engineers with a bias toward practical, production-proven results, and develop the leaders within it. Own the technical roadmap. Partner with various other security teams and infrastructure engineering to architect the roadmap for EDA-specific security controls and ship them into production.
Make the network and platform your control plane. Protection doesn’t depend just on what’s running inside the node.
Engineer around hard constraints. Determine where conventional endpoint and workload security tooling fits, where it doesn’t, and design the alternative: security that protects multi-day compute jobs without degrading them.
Make enforcement uniform. Drive consistent application of security frameworks across on-prem data centers and multi-cloud platforms where “consistent” means enforced, not documented.
Run the full lifecycle of core infrastructure security technologies: selection, deployment, operation, and eventual replacement.
Automate the evidence. Build the KPIs, instrumentation, and audit workflows that make security posture across EDA systems continuously visible treating compliance evidence as an engineering output, not a manual exercise.
Think like an adversary. Mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute.
Champion security by design, embedding automation and secure defaults into the infrastructure lifecycle instead of bolting them on afterward.

What We Need To See

12+ overall years building and operating production infrastructure at scale - network, compute clusters, and storage including 5+ years leading and managing engineering teams. A Bachelor’s degree in a relevant engineering field or equivalent experience.
Deep networking expertise applied to large compute environments.
Hands-on depth operating compute fleets at scale - provisioning, lifecycle, and the operational realities of long-running, high-value jobs.
Deep understanding of hyperscaler methodologies for operating large-scale systems with security and reliability as co-equal goals.
Experience securing performance-sensitive or high-throughput environments where standard agent-based tooling was constrained and you engineered a workable answer.
Extensive history of building and guiding engineering teams responsible for complex distributed or multi-cloud architectures.
Demonstrated ability to drive unified outcomes across organizational boundaries, with partners who do not report to you.
Exceptional communication skills credible with individual engineers and executive leadership in the same day.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Built or operated infrastructure security capabilities at a hyperscaler or a security product company — you’ve engineered detection and enforcement systems, not just deployed someone else’s.
Experience with kernel- and fabric-level observability and enforcement - eBPF, in-line and out-of-band inspection, DPU/SmartNIC offload - as an alternative to heavyweight in-node agents.
Track record leading security or platform engineering inside EDA, HPC, or large research-cluster environments. Breadth across security domains - IAM, EDR/XDR, CNAPP, CSPM, vulnerability lifecycle, zero-trust architectures - or a demonstrated pattern of picking up new domains fast.
Experience driving infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state rather than an audited one, plus familiarity translating SOC2 / ISO27001 into real technical controls.

NVIDIA is leading the way in groundbreaking developments in Artificial Intelligence, High-Performance Computing, and Visualization. Our invention serves as the visual cortex of modern computers and is at the heart of our products and services. Our work opens up new universes to explore, enables amazing creativity and discovery, and powers what were once science fiction inventions from artificial intelligence to autonomous cars. NVIDIA is seeking exceptional individuals like you to help us drive the next wave of artificial intelligence.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 272,000 USD - 431,250 USD for Level 4, and 320,000 USD - 488,750 USD for Level 5.

Thousands of hardware engineers designing next-generation silicon depend on it being fast, available, and frictionless and when it isn’t, tapeout schedules feel it. This team is the difference. We’re hiring a hands-on engineering leader to develop our Global Customer Engineering for Internal EDA Infrastructure - the organization sitting directly between our chip designers and the platforms they run on. The Kubernetes platform team that delivers one of our customer services end to end.

Make enforcement uniform. Drive consistent application of security frameworks across on-prem data centers and multi-cloud platforms where “consistent” means enforced, not documented.
Run the full lifecycle of core infrastructure security technologies: selection, deployment, operation, and eventual replacement.
Automate the evidence. Build the KPIs, instrumentation, and audit workflows that make security posture across EDA systems continuously visible treating compliance evidence as an engineering output, not a manual exercise.
Think like an adversary. Mitigation planning across network, storage, and compute.
Champion security by design, embedding automation and secure defaults into the infrastructure lifecycle instead of bolting them on afterward.

What We Need To See

12+ overall years building and operating production infrastructure at scale - network, compute clusters, and storage including 5+ years leading and managing engineering teams. A Bachelor’s degree in a relevant engineering field or equivalent experience.
Deep networking expertise applied to large compute environments.
Hands-on depth operating compute fleets at scale - provisioning, lifecycle, and the operational realities of long-running, high-value jobs.
Deep understanding of hyperscaler methodologies for operating large-scale systems with security and reliability as co-equal goals.
Experience securing performance-sensitive or high-throughput environments where standard agent-based tooling was constrained and you engineered a workable answer.
Extensive history of building and guiding engineering teams responsible for complex distributed or multi-cloud architectures.
Demonstrated ability to drive unified outcomes across organizational boundaries, with partners who do not report to you.
Exceptional communication skills credible with individual engineers and executive leadership in the same day.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Built or operated infrastructure security capabilities at a hyperscaler or a security product company — you’ve engineered detection and enforcement systems, not just deployed someone else’s.
Experience with kernel- and fabric-level observability and enforcement - eBPF, in-line and out-of-band inspection, DPU/SmartNIC offload - as an alternative to heavyweight in-node agents.
Track record leading security or platform engineering inside EDA, HPC, or large research-cluster environments. Breadth across security domains - IAM, EDR/XDR, CNAPP, CSPM, vulnerability lifecycle, zero-trust architectures - or a demonstrated pattern of picking up new domains fast.
Experience driving infrastructure-as-code and policy-as-code so secure configuration is the default state rather than an audited one, plus familiarity translating SOC2 / ISO27001 into real technical controls.

Every NVIDIA GPU starts as a job on our internal EDA infrastructure. Thousands of hardware engineers designing next-generation silicon depend on it being fast, available, and frictionless and when it isn’t, tapeout schedules feel it. This team is the difference. We’re hiring a hands-on engineering leader to develop our Global Customer Engineering for Internal EDA Infrastructure - the organization sitting directly between our chip designers and the platforms they run on. This is a multi-team leadership role spanning managers and tech leads across a globally distributed organization, and it comes with two co-equal mandates: A world-class customer engineering organization for EDA infrastructure - reactive when it must be, proactive by design. The Kubernetes platform team that delivers one of our customer services end to end.

You will design software solutions, and automation pipelines to eliminate operational overhead. When encountering recurring toil for customer engineering, your immediate impulse is to engineer permanent automated remedies. Staying directly connected to live production environments is essential hence the end-to-end Kubernetes platform responsibility.

What You’ll Be Doing

Build the leaders. Grow and develop the leaders running a globally distributed team of customer-facing engineers who own the reactive support queue for EDA infrastructure - escalating into service engineering with clean, high-quality signal.
Develop the Kubernetes platform. Run the K8s platform team as a first-class customer engineering service: availability, roadmap, developer experience, and the operational excellence behind it.
Ship the L0 AI support layer. Own the evolution of our AI support agent from FAQ bot to a system that safely resolves real issues against real internal systems - and measurably removes volume from human queues.
Set the bar. Define and defend SLOs for operational performance, and win genuine stakeholder buy-in.
Stay close to the metal. Drive deep support and continuous improvement across EDA job schedulers (LSF/Slurm), Kubernetes platforms, and the internal LLM harnesses our chip designers depend on.

What We Need To See

12+ overall years building and leading engineering support organizations, spanning reactive and proactive customer engineering.
5+ years of experience leading a globally distributed organization, including developing managers and leaders.
Proven ability to influence technical roadmaps by turning support trends into engineering requirements that actually ship.
Deep technical familiarity with Kubernetes, EDA workloads, job schedulers, and AI/LLM infrastructure foundations.
Track record of leveraging automation and AI/ML to improve support efficiency and drive ticket volume down.
Exceptional communication skills - credible with individual engineers and executive leadership in the same day.
A Bachelor’s degree in a relevant engineering field or equivalent experience.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Led a platform team and a customer facing team simultaneously, and made each one better because of the other.
You’ve architected “self-healing” support ecosystems where a customer engineering team builds and owns the tools it runs on including “shift-left” tooling that resolved issues before a ticket ever existed.
You’ve led the full lifecycle of generative AI / LLM-based support assistants, well beyond basic chatbots, into systems that integrate deeply and safely with internal infrastructure.
Run LSF, Slurm, or Kubernetes at a scale where manual intervention was the bottleneck and you personally led the automation that removed it.

Partnering directly with executive leaders in Product, Design, Finance, and Infrastructure, you will transform complex, distributed database capabilities into an effortless, intuitive, and wildly reliable cloud service.

Drive Technical Excellence: Serve as the ultimate bar-raiser for microservices architecture, API design, and modern frontend systems. Keep the tech stack cutting-edge while eliminating complexity.
Align Tech with Business Growth: Translate big-picture enterprise strategy into clear, executable technical roadmaps alongside Product, Revenue, and Executive Leadership.
Own Production Reliability: Establish non-negotiable standards for billing precision, sub-second interface performance, and enterprise-grade SLA availability in a 24/7/365 cloud environment.

What We’re Looking For

10+ years scaling customer-facing SaaS, PaaS, or cloud infrastructure platforms at serious velocity.
4+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience, with a proven track record of managing managers, scaling teams, and leading through technical leads.
Domain Powerhouse: Deep expertise in architecting cloud monetization engines (metered billing, marketplace integrations) and high-throughput telemetry/observability platforms (OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Prometheus).
Deep Technical DNA: Hands-on foundation in modern web stacks (React, TypeScript), scalable API design (REST, GraphQL), and cloud-native infrastructure (Kubernetes, Go, multi-cloud platforms).
Executive Presence & Business Acumen: A clear, compelling communicator who seamlessly connects deep technical architecture to revenue strategy, product execution, and executive goals.

Direct experience leading engineering through periods of rapid scaling, enterprise transformations, or major cloud platform expansions.
Hands-on familiarity with distributed systems, event-driven architectures, or technologies like Temporal and Node.js.
Familiarity with distributed systems or high-scale databases.

: $272,000 – $350,000

Role Summary

The Director, AI & Automation leads the team responsible for building and scaling the organization's automation and agentic AI capabilities. This role owns a team of engineers working across two closely related domains: workflow orchestration and deterministic automation, and agentic coding practices and AI-enabled engineering.

This is a high-autonomy, high-accountability role at the leading edge of how the organization applies AI to internal operations. The Director is expected to be a practitioner and a leader - someone who understands the technology deeply enough to make good engineering decisions, develop strong engineers, and contribute meaningfully to how the organization thinks about AI adoption and governance over time.

Essential Functions

Lead a team of engineers across agentic AI and workflow automation disciplines, organized into self-directed pods aligned to business domains; ensure pods are staffed, enabled, and delivering effectively.
Own engineering quality and technical standards across both workflow orchestration and deterministic automation, as well as agentic AI tooling and practices.
Drive adoption of agentic coding practices across the team - establishing patterns, evaluating emerging approaches, and building engineering fluency in AI-assisted development at scale.
Partner with Product Owners embedded in each pod to ensure engineers have clear priorities, well-defined work, and the technical context needed to deliver effectively.
Ensure continuous rapid evaluation of automation tooling, frameworks, and agentic patterns, bringing well-reasoned recommendations to leadership and contributing to governance conversations as a technical voice.
Participate in AI governance and definition of responsible AI frameworks, helping to establish standards for how the organization deploys, monitors, and evaluates AI-driven automation in production.
Manage the full engineer lifecycle across the team - hiring, onboarding, performance, growth, and retention - with particular attention to developing engineers in a fast-moving and ambiguous technology domain.
Maintain visibility into pod delivery across all business domains; surface risks, capacity issues, and cross-pod dependencies to leadership before they become blockers.
Represent the AI & Intelligent Automation engineering function in cross-functional conversations with technology leadership, business stakeholders, and vendor partners.

Qualifications & Skills

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field. Equivalent experience accepted.

Demonstrated ability to lead engineers or technical teams working in fast-moving, ambiguous domains where standards and practices are still being established.
